title: Neutron Interferometry
description: A neutron is a wave too. Split it with a perfect crystal, let gravity pull on one path a little more than the other, and the waves no longer meet in step: gravity, measured on a single quantum particle. Unlocks the Neutron Interferometer and the Silicon Boule.

puzzle.goal: A neutron of mass m and wavelength λ is split into two paths that enclose an area A, the plane of the paths tilted by α. Gravity g changes the higher path's momentum; write the phase difference φ that builds up between them, from the quantum of action h.
puzzle.name: Gravitationally induced quantum phase
puzzle.form: 2 * π * m ^ 2 * g * λ * A * sin ( α ) / h ^ 2
puzzle.ask: Find φ in radians for m = 1.675e-27 kg, g = @{g} m/s², L = @{L} m, A = @{A} m², a = @{a} rad (30°), h = 6.626e-34 J·s.
puzzle.method: Climbing a height H costs the neutron mgH of kinetic energy, so its wavenumber falls by m²gHλ/h²·2π; over a path length L at that height, the phases part by that times L - and H·L = A·sin α.
